title: Child-care work prevention and reported time-loss type differ across stable SNAP states
source_unit: identified person with November-to-December adjacent-month SNAP pair and annual fall child-care fields

observations.period: 2024 reference year; November-to-December stable no-SNAP pair

denominator.unit: valid person transition pairs for EWORKMORE

time_lost_hours_share.unit: percent of valid reported time-loss cases

time_lost_days_share.unit: percent of valid reported time-loss cases

time_lost_weeks_share.unit: percent of valid reported time-loss cases

observations.method: Same-person November-to-December SNAP transition paired with December-carried annual fall child-care fields; WPFINWGT with 240 Fay-BRR replicate weights and perturbation factor 0.5.
observations.uncertainty: A flag-inclusive rerun using AWORKMORE, ATIMELOST, and ATIMELOST_TP produced the same point estimates and valid-cell counts as the response-code audit. The time-loss denominator is only 71 records. Child-care fields refer to the fall reference year and are not monthly December outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Persons in stable no-SNAP November-to-December transitions; annual child-care fields describe reference parents and have separate universes.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stable SNAP status may mark different household composition, eligibility, employment, care needs, or resources; this comparison does not estimate a SNAP effect or show that time loss was caused by the program.

related_sources.claim: The SIPP dictionary defines EWORKMORE, ETIMELOST, and ETIMELOST_TP and their fall-reference-year universes.
Prior child-care payment, assistance, and work-prevention comparison using the same transition design.

reproduction_audit.result: Exact point estimates and standard errors reproduced for all four transition groups and all reported metrics; entry/exit care-prevention cells remained 4 and 2 with no valid time-loss cases.
reproduction_audit.interpretation: Reproduction confirms the committed descriptive layer, not a causal SNAP estimate. Raw inputs remain outside the repository.

boundary: This is a same-person timing bridge across adjacent SNAP status and annual fall child-care measures. It strengthens the material-support-to-work/care-time arrow, but it does not establish a program effect, exact event timing, hours lost, notice/effort, care quality, household outcome, trust, political action, or recovery. Entry and exit cells are too sparse for time-loss reporting.
